title: Port registry bidirectional mismatch — two workspaces, one port (xanadu-core_b case)
description: Reproduction: xanadu-core_b workspace URL served xanadu_b's shells. Root cause: registry.workspaces[xanadu-core_b] had currentPort=8164 (stale, from a container that exited 41h ago) while registry.ports[8164] pointed to xanadu_b. Proxy routed xanadu-core_b requests to 8164 → xanadu_b's container. Mitigated by manually removing the stale workspace entry. Chained allocation in allocatePort would prevent this if it were always used, but some code path (likely blue-green recreation or updatePortInRegistry) writes entries without probing for collisions. This is exactly the ym4 (port consolidation) motivation. Also, the container for xanadu-core_b exited cleanly without cleanupIdleContainers removing its registry entry — a known gap. Fix: Phase 3 (8bx) already covers this (PortRegistry.reconcile + release from cleanupIdleContainers).
notes:
SMOKING GUN (from journal logs):

Apr 19 02:22:16 — TWO "Allocated port 8164" messages for different instances (xanadu_b and xanadu-core_b) in the SAME SECOND. Classic concurrent allocation race.

Both requests loaded the same registry snapshot, both called allocatePort. xanadu-core_b hashed to 8164 directly. xanadu_b hashed to 8163, probed to 8164. Both saw 8164 as free in their in-memory copies. Both wrote to registry, last write wins — but workspaces[] entries for different paths don't overwrite each other, only the shared ports[8164] reverse mapping does.

02:22:17: docker bind 0.0.0.0:8164 failed for xanadu-core_b container — but registry already has the duplicate claim.

02:22:34: cleanupStaleEntries detected xanadu_b registry=8165 (?) vs container=8164 and 'updated' registry, further tangling state.

Fix plan confirmed:
A. cleanupStaleEntries shouldn't destroy entries on transient failure.
B. getOrAllocatePort needs defensive ports[port] check before overwrite.
C. REQUIRED: serialize port allocation with a process-wide mutex, since instanceLocks are keyed per-instance and don't guard between different workspaces. This is the primary root cause.
close_reason: Root cause isolated from journal logs: concurrent getOrAllocatePort calls for different workspaces both loaded the same registry snapshot and both allocated port 8164 in the same second. instanceLocks did not serialize across different workspaces. Fixed in commit 35243c7 via registryMutex (serializes all port-registry mutations), hardened getContainerPort/cleanupStaleEntries (no destruction on transient errors), and defensive invariant checks before all reverse-mapping writes. Registry manually cleaned of the pre-existing collision.

title: Fix duplicate adoption: creationOptions.env stripped on restore
description: Log shows restored terminals fire onDidOpenTerminal with paneId=- and session=- — code-server does NOT preserve creationOptions.env across extension host restart. terminalSession() returns null, adoptOrphans treats the session as uncovered and adopts it, creating a duplicate. Fix: fallback to reading /proc/<terminal.processId>/environ to recover TMUX_SESSION/TMUX_PANE_ID from the preserved host-bash process env. Cache the result per terminal. Log evidence: 2026-04-13T13:31:30 onDidOpenTerminal with empty env; 13:31:55 adoptOrphans duplicates the session.
close_reason: Closed

title: Redesign terminal tracking: live VS Code terminals as source of truth
description: Replace reconnectMapped + adoptUnmappedSessions + canonicalizeMapping with a single reconcile() function that treats vscode.window.terminals as the source of truth. Identifies session per terminal via creationOptions.env.TMUX_SESSION (fallback: resolveSession via cs-tmux-window). Invariant: at most one VS Code terminal per live tmux session. Disposes duplicates, adopts orphans. Refcount guard in onDidCloseTerminal kills session only when no VS Code terminal remains viewing it. See tmp/issues/terminal-session-tracking/redesign.md for full design.
close_reason: Closed

title: Canonicalize and dedup mapping to fix persistent duplicate terminals
description: 3f5b0ae fix (scan vscode.window.terminals at activation) didn't handle the case where mapping.panes had stale duplicates from past runs — two paneIds resolving to the same tmux session, persisted across reloads. reconnectMapped faithfully created a terminal for each. Closing one killed the shared session and took the other down. Fix: canonicalizeMapping() populates missing tmuxSession via resolveSession, drops gone sessions, dedups by preferring panes with live terminals. Called at start of reconnectMapped and each adoptUnmappedSessions run. Committed 22c81de.
close_reason: Committed 22c81de. canonicalizeMapping resolves/drops/dedups entries before reconnectMapped and adoptUnmappedSessions.

title: Fix duplicate terminals on extension restart with restored terminals
description: On Developer: Reload Window (and likely other extension host restarts), code-server preserves the PTY processes of extension-profile-created terminals. When the extension reactivates, reconnectMapped runs BEFORE code-server surfaces the restored terminals — so terminalToPaneId Map is empty, existingPaneIds check in reconnectMapped misses restored terminals, and the extension creates a duplicate terminal for each mapped pane. Closing one of the duplicate pair kills the shared tmux session (via paneInfo.tmuxSession cache) and takes the other terminal with it, irretrievably. Fix: in reconnectMapped (or earlier in activate), scan vscode.window.terminals and extract TMUX_PANE_ID from creationOptions.env to pre-populate the existingPaneIds set and terminalToPaneId Map before creating new terminals.
close_reason: Committed 3f5b0ae. Root cause: reconnectMapped ran before code-server surfaced restored terminals, creating duplicates. Fix: scan vscode.window.terminals at reconnectMapped start, register restored terminals with TMUX_PANE_ID from creationOptions.env, cache their tmuxSession. Added defensive refcount in removePaneFromMapping to prevent killing session if another pane still references it.

title: Fix tmux leak: populate paneInfo.tmuxSession via cs-tmux-window resolve
description: Root cause (confirmed by instrumentation, see code-server-proxy-ebl): extensions/tmux-session-manager/src/extension.ts savePaneToMapping initializes paneInfo.tmuxSession='' with a comment 'filled by host-bash via cs-tmux-window', but NOTHING ever fills it. host-bash writes only to cs-tmux-window's host-side mapping (~/.config/code-server-proxy/mappings/cs-{iid}.json), not to the extension's workspace-storage mapping. Consequences: (1) removePaneFromMapping's 'if (paneInfo?.tmuxSession) killTmuxSession(...)' guard never fires — every tracked Host Shell terminal leaks its session on close. (2) reconnectMapped treats every mapped pane as 'session gone' and wipes the mapping. (3) 'Reconnect All' command always reports 0. H1 (exit-reason filter wrong) is refuted; reason=User fires correctly on tab close, but kill branch short-circuits on empty string. Fix: add 'resolve <iid> <pane-id>' subcommand to host/bin/cs-tmux-window that reads the host-side mapping and prints the session name. Change removePaneFromMapping to query it via SSH, then call killTmuxSession unconditionally. Also fix reconnectMapped to query-and-populate tmuxSession rather than relying on an always-empty field. Instrumentation confirmed session cs-adfa2166…-11 created 22:37:34 on explicit tab-X close at 22:37:38 reason=User still present 12+ minutes later.
close_reason: Fix committed as b977d0b. Root cause was paneInfo.tmuxSession always being empty string; extension never called killTmuxSession. Added cs-tmux-window resolve subcommand; extension now queries host-side mapping on pane close and kills the actual session. Verified on xa-optimize: closing a tracked Host Shell (tmux) emitted kill log and session was confirmed gone from host tmux ls. H1 (exit-reason filter) refuted during investigation.

title: Raise tmux server fd limit persistently
description: Current soft limit is 1024. Raised temporarily to 65536 via prlimit, but will reset on tmux server restart. Need persistent fix: set ulimit -n 65536 where the tmux server is first spawned (ssh login shell, systemd user session, or wrapper around first tmux new-session call). Verify via cat /proc/$(pgrep tmux)/limits after next restart. See tmp/issues/tmux-leak/plan.md P0.1.
close_reason: Added ulimit -n 65536 at top of cs-tmux-window. New tmux servers inherit the higher limit. Running server was already raised via prlimit. Committed b700888.

title: Instrument onDidCloseTerminal exit reasons in tmux-session-manager
description: Hypothesis H1: sessions leak because code-server does not emit TerminalExitReason.User on explicit tab-X close, so removePaneFromMapping never runs and sessions are never killed. Added logging of terminal.exitStatus.reason to extensions/tmux-session-manager/src/extension.ts (onDidCloseTerminal handler), deployed to code-server-extensions shared volume via docker cp. Reload a code-server instance, open/close terminal tabs in several scenarios (tab-X, browser reload, code-server restart), collect log output from code-server output channel, and determine what reasons are actually emitted. This blocks the fix for H1. See tmp/issues/tmux-leak/plan.md P1.3.
close_reason: Fix committed as b977d0b. cs-tmux-window gained resolve subcommand; extension now queries host-side mapping on pane close and kills the actual session. Verified on code-server-61f52b7f (xa-optimize): closing a tracked Host Shell (tmux) terminal emitted kill log and session was confirmed gone from host tmux ls.

title: Make tmux orphan sweep robust under fd pressure
description: cleanOrphanedTmuxSessions in src/container-manager.js silently swallows errors from 'tmux list-sessions', which is exactly the call that fails when tmux hits its fd limit. Result: the one mechanism that could recover from leaks is disabled precisely when it is most needed. Fix: log (not swallow) list-sessions errors; if it fails, escalate (alert, attempt cleanup of oldest idle sessions, or let proxy restart). Also stop silently returning when port-registry is unreadable. See tmp/issues/tmux-leak/plan.md P0.2.
close_reason: Committed eef8489. Orphan sweep now logs list-sessions failures, registry read failures, and warns at >200 sessions.

title: tmux session leak — fd exhaustion at 1024 limit
description: Host tmux server accumulated 334 sessions and hit soft fd limit (1024), causing 'open terminal failed: not a terminal' in all host shells and hanging new terminals. Mitigated by raising limit via prlimit to 65536 on running tmux server. See tmp/issues/tmux-leak/plan.md for full investigation and design discussion. Parent epic tracking all follow-ups.
close_reason: All blockers resolved. Root cause: extension never populated paneInfo.tmuxSession, so killTmuxSession was never called. Fix: cs-tmux-window resolve subcommand + extension queries it on close (b977d0b). Persistent fd limit (b700888). Robust orphan sweep with logging (eef8489). Per-instance + fd-pressure monitoring (fa5484b). Cleaned up 313 leaked sessions (411→98). Only v54 (idle-session reaping) deferred.

title: Consolidate port allocation into single authority
description: Port logic is scattered: allocatePort, getOrAllocatePort, updatePortInRegistry, blue-green step 7, cleanupStaleEntries. Each manipulates the bidirectional registry.workspaces/registry.ports mapping independently, causing collisions (xa-adapt/xanadu-core_b both on 8164). Need one PortRegistry class/module that owns all reads/writes to the registry, ensures bidirectional consistency, and is the single place that allocates/frees/swaps ports.

close_reason: Blue-green recreation implemented: temp container boots on temp port, port registry swaps atomically, containers rename, old stops. Active containers get blue-green, idle get simple stop-remove.

Extension manages pane-to-window mapping and layout restore. See tmp/issues/tmux/analysis.md for full design.

Improve UX when VSCode WebSocket reconnection fails. Instead of showing "Cannot reconnect. Please reload the window." dialog, automatically reload the page to restore the session.

1. Client-side JS script injected into pages - monitors for reconnection failure dialog
2. Proxy modification to inject script into HTML responses from code-server

title: Extension rebuilds never deployed — no install step into shared code-server-extensions volume
description:
code-server instances load the tmux-session-manager extension from the shared Docker volume (config.docker.sharedExtensionsVolume='code-server-extensions'), but nothing in the repo deploys a rebuilt extension there. Committing a rebuilt vsix does NOT update running instances. This caused code-server-proxy-58o (show teammate name on adopted tabs) to appear 'done' in git for days while every instance kept loading the stale April build (which still hardcoded 'Host Shell (tmux)'). The fix only became live after manually running 'code-server --install-extension --force' against the volume.

Fix: scripts/install-extension.sh added — builds (compile+package) and installs the vsix into the volume as the host uid. Follow-ups to consider: wire it into the build, document the reload-required step, and ensure rayon deploy runs it so the new server gets the current build.

Note on existing tabs: even after deploy+reload, already-open tabs keep their old name (VS Code has no rename-in-place API; the extension names terminals only at creation). Existing terminals are restored by code-server persistence and re-claim their sessions, so adoptOrphans never recreates them. Only newly created tabs / re-adopted orphan sessions get the resolved name.
notes: Related: code-server-proxy-58o (the feature that was undeployed). The deploy gap, not the feature code, is the bug here.

title: Show teammate/session name on adopted tmux tabs (currently hardcoded 'Host Shell (tmux)')
description:
createTerminalForSession (extensions/tmux-session-manager/src/extension.ts:381) hardcodes name:'Host Shell (tmux)' for every adopted tab (paneInfo.name :385 and createTerminal name :393), so all teammate panes (wedge/nursery/blockerr) display the same constant instead of their name.

Fix (A) — recommended, name lives with the session: launch-teammate (~/bin) runs 'tmux rename-window -t cs-<iid>-N <teammate>' at creation; createTerminalForSession fetches the window name (tmux display-message -p -t <session> '#W') via the existing host-bash/SSH path it already uses in resolveSession (extension.ts:176), and passes it as createTerminal({name}), falling back to 'Host Shell (tmux)'. ~10 lines in the extension + 1 line in launch-teammate. Durable across re-adoption (name stored in tmux). Needs extension rebuild + code-server window reload.

Fix (B) — no rebuild: set code-server 'terminal.integrated.tabs.title: ${sequence}' and emit the name as the OSC title from each teammate's tmux session (set -g set-titles on; set-titles-string '#W'; rename-window <teammate>). Lighter, but whether ${sequence} overrides the explicit createTerminal name varies by code-server build — needs testing.

Recommend (A). Related: ~/bin/launch-teammate + cs-tab, and the launch-teammate Claude skill.
close_reason: Adopted tmux tabs now show the teammate/session name. createTerminalForSession fetches the tmux window name via 'tmux display-message -p -t <session> #W' over the existing host-bash/SSH path and uses it as the terminal name, falling back to 'Host Shell (tmux)' for default/unnamed shell windows (bash/host-bash/sh/empty). The window is already renamed to the teammate name at creation by cs-tab (called by launch-teammate with -n NAME) and persists because automatic-rename is off in tmux.conf, so no launch-teammate edit was needed — the rename single-sources in cs-tab. Extension recompiled + vsix repackaged; needs code-server window reload to load.

title: Container bound to stale port must be recreated, not looped
description: Reproduced 2026-04-21 02:29 after fixing 5ga. xanadu-core_b's container had Docker PortBindings pointing at 8164 (from a prior failed bind) but registry was correctly re-allocated to 8165. Proxy routes to 8165 → no container there → loop. cleanupStaleEntries correctly refuses to clobber xanadu_b's claim on 8164, but the container is effectively unreachable. Manually resolved by docker stop+rm. Root cause: there's no code path that says 'container's port disagrees with registry AND the container port is owned by another workspace → recreate the container'. launchInstance should detect this at start time and recreate if port bindings don't match the registry-assigned port. Even simpler: always check container port matches assigned port at start; if not, remove and recreate. See journal at 2026-04-21T02:29 for log of the loop.
close_reason: Committed deadf1b. launchInstanceUnsafe now compares container's actual Docker PortBindings to the assigned port at launch time; if they differ, stops and removes the container before recreating. Volume persists so workspace state is preserved. Reproduced with xanadu-core_b and manually remediated; next time the recreation will be automatic.

title: Mystery host-bash terminal still spawns new session on reload
description: After commit 3f12bce (defer initial adoption to periodic interval), terminals still appear ~30s after reload. A mystery terminal with empty name and shellPath=/usr/local/bin/host-bash appears shortly after activation; its creator is unknown (grep host-bash in /config/extensions returns only our own extension). Its host-bash runs cs-tmux-window grab which creates a new tmux session when no unattached session is available. 3f12bce was meant to let grab find the prior unattached session before we adopt, but user reports terminals still appearing after 30s. Investigate: 1) is the mystery terminal's session being identified via ssh-child cmdline but still adopted (parser regression); 2) or is it still creating new sessions because all sessions are attached by the time its grab runs; 3) is the creator something other than an extension (code-server core, terminal profile config, VS Code built-in). Test with two reloads in quick succession and compare tmux session count.
close_reason: Committed 9abc19e. Creator identified: ms-python.python's env-discovery uses createTerminal({shellPath: appEnv.shell, hideFromUser: true}). With SHELL=/usr/local/bin/host-bash inherited from the container env, the hidden shell was host-bash, which took the interactive path and grabbed/created a tmux session. When the hidden terminal exited, the session became unattached → adoptOrphans 30s later made it a visible tab. Fix: track hideFromUser terminals in an ephemeralTerminals WeakSet at onDidOpenTerminal; on close, kill the tmux session unconditionally (no refcount guard). No more ghost tabs after reload.

title: Extract config.js consolidating all env vars and constants

Create src/config.js that reads and validates all env vars once at startup. Export a frozen config object. Modules import from config.js instead of reading process.env directly. Validates required vars, applies defaults, logs the effective configuration. Not DI — just a config object. See tmp/issues/port-consolidation/plan.md Q1.
close_reason: Committed 4f66920. Created src/config.js consolidating all env vars: INSTANCES_BASE_PATH (was in 3 files), HOME-derived paths (4 files), Docker config, idle thresholds, timer intervals. All modules now import from config. Object is frozen. Zero process.env reads outside config.js.

title: Extension's listTmuxSessions fails DNS inside extension host
description: extensions/tmux-session-manager/src/extension.ts listTmuxSessions() calls execSync('ssh ... host.docker.internal ...') every 30s from the auto-adopt interval. In at least one code-server container (adfa2166…, xa-opt-kkt workspace), this consistently logs 'ssh: Could not resolve hostname host.docker.internal: Name or service not known' every 30s to the Window log. Verified from a docker-exec shell in the same container: /etc/hosts has the entry, getent resolves it, ssh command works, and even Node execSync of the same command works. Yet the extension host's execSync fails. Container's extension host was started with --dns-result-order=ipv4first. Affects auto-adopt (orphan surfacing) but not terminal creation. Longstanding preexisting bug, discovered during tmux-leak instrumentation.
close_reason: Not a functional bug. SSH with ControlMaster=auto prints a DNS resolution error to stderr before falling through to the existing control socket. The connection succeeds (exit 0) and stdout has correct data. Confirmed by diagnostic command: dns.lookup succeeds, ssh -vvv succeeds (exit 0 despite stderr DNS error), ssh without ControlMaster also succeeds. The stderr noise is logged by code-server as [error] [Extension Host] which looks alarming but is cosmetic. Two OpenSSH versions (13.14 vs 13.15) suggest the control master was started before a package update, causing the speculative DNS check to behave differently.

title: Clean up existing leaked tmux sessions on host

Orphaned instances (3): 15e02c4d…, 3cd8a9d5…, 6aa97dbc… — safe to cs-tmux-window cleanup. Live-container leaks: NOT safe to blind-kill; distinguish in-use from leaked (e.g. kill idle > 24h where session_activity == session_created) or coordinate with user to close workspaces. Do not run until P0 and P1 fixes are deployed — cleanup without root-cause fix would just repeat. See tmp/issues/tmux-leak/plan.md 'Cleanup of current leak'.
close_reason: Killed 23 sessions from 2 orphaned instances (no live container), then 292 never-used sessions older than 24h across all live containers. 411 → 98 sessions remaining. Of the 98: 76 have real user activity, 25 are < 24h old. tmux fd usage 347/65536.

close_reason: Systemd timer at 6am restarts containers with extension host RSS > 1GB. Script checks all extension hosts, restarts matching containers. tmux sessions survive.

title: Shells assigned to wrong workspaces on simultaneous reconnect from sleep
WebSocket connections become stale after hours, require page reload (1006)
Zombie host-bash processes attached to nonexistent tmux sessions
description: Observed in container code-server-aee4ca47…: 2 host-bash processes stuck in do_poll, their ssh -t child attempting to attach to tmux sessions that have already been killed (cs-…-0, cs-…-21). The sessions are gone from tmux ls but the ssh processes remain alive with live SSH sockets. Normally when tmux kills a session with a client attached, the client (tmux attach) exits, ssh -t exits, host-bash's reconnect loop detects via has-session and breaks. Something in that chain is not completing. Minor fd/port leak. Possibly related to ControlMaster multiplexing behavior when a session is killed externally. Discovered during canonicalize investigation.
